topics.name: LLM-Induced Psychosis and Cognitive Security
topics.summary: Hosts discussed emerging reports of users developing psychosis after extended LLM sessions, often combined with drug use or predispositions to mental illness; compared the phenomenon to early social media harms and the Bing Sydney chatbot incident; called for fast guardrail action from AI labs.

topics.name: Genius Act Stablecoin Bill Signing
topics.summary: Kyle Samani reported live from DC on President Trump signing the Genius Act, described as the most consequential financial legislation since Dodd-Frank; argued stablecoins could enable 5–6 billion people globally to hold USD for the first time, representing a historic capital movement.

topics.name: AI Researcher Talent Wars
topics.summary: Meta poaching OpenAI researchers at $100–200M packages; discussion of the broader talent concentration phenomenon across finance, media, and AI research where individual talent captures disproportionate value and equity returns suffer.

topics.name: Quantum Computing Stocks
topics.summary: Martin Shkreli argued quantum computing stocks are overvalued shorts; quantum computers run at ~100 kHz, IBM's best is 135 qubits, and Shor's algorithm is the only meaningful speedup algorithm—without a new breakthrough, there is no commercial case.

topics.name: Bloomberg Terminal Disruption
topics.summary: Shkreli's new startup is building a Bloomberg competitor with millions in ARR; argued Bloomberg has no quant offering, is an entry-level tool for top hedge funds, and a well-run replacement could be worth a trillion dollars.

topics.name: Arc AGI V3 Public Preview
topics.summary: Mike Knoop previewed the first three public games of Arc AGI V3, an interactive game-based benchmark with 64×64 grids and efficiency limits; a $10,000 agent contest was launched; described as significantly harder than V1 and V2 and LLM-resistant by design.

topics.name: Range Rover Logo Redesign
topics.summary: Range Rover's first logo mark in 55 years—a double-R design—generated broadly negative reactions on social media, with commenters finding it confusing and derivative.

topics.name: Nextdoor Product Relaunch
topics.summary: Nirav Tolia returned as refounder and launched a major redesign Wednesday, moving from an all-purpose newsfeed to structured surfaces for local news, alerts, and recommendations; has 100M+ verified neighbors and is planning disaster response and local politician integrations.

topics.name: Substack Series C and Going Direct Debate
topics.summary: Chris Best announced a $100M Series C via a New York Times exclusive, prompting debate about whether going to legacy media to announce is antithetical to Substack's mission or strategically smart for recruiting new creators from the NYT readership.

topics.name: Federal Reserve Chair Succession
topics.summary: Joe Weisenthal discussed Kevin Warsh, Kevin Hassett, and Christopher Waller as potential Powell replacements; warned that rate cuts could paradoxically raise mortgage rates if the long end of the yield curve rises on inflation expectations.

topics.name: China vs. US Open Source AI Competition
topics.summary: Jeremy from Semi Analysis (prior episode) noted China leads open-source AI across DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot, and Manus; hosts discussed whether the US can maintain leadership given Meta's open-source uncertainty.

topics.name: ChatGPT Agent Launch
topics.summary: Swix argued the ChatGPT Agent launch contains a frontier model that effectively constitutes GPT-5 without the version bump; praised it for combining a browser, terminal, and computer use into a single unified agent.

topics.name: Bitcoin Cryptographic Vulnerability
topics.summary: Shkreli outlined three attack vectors on Bitcoin: brute force relying on Moore's Law, mathematical hacks on elliptic curve cryptography, and AI-assisted cryptographic research; noted Satoshi's P2PK-format early wallets are most vulnerable because they expose the elliptic curve x-coordinate.

topics.name: High Frequency Trading, Quant Finance, and AI
topics.summary: Shkreli argued quant trading methods from top firms like Renaissance are no longer secret, and AI will allow more traders to access quant strategies; discussed the idea of an AI-powered trading engine that could generate $100B+ in profits like a 'machine god.'

topics.name: Legacy Enterprise Tech Migration and AI
topics.summary: Discussed whether AI coding agents like Claude Code and Devin can automate Python 2 to Python 3 migrations; concluded that ERP-level migrations remain extremely complex and expensive even with AI assistance due to context window limits and test suite complexity.

topics.name: Power Laws in Talent Compensation
topics.summary: Joe Weisenthal and hosts discussed the expanding winner-take-all phenomenon: top AI researchers, star podcasters, and elite traders capturing extraordinary individual compensation while equity shareholders get less; contrasted with network-effect businesses like Instagram where talent is more interchangeable.

topics.name: AI-Generated Entertainment and Jailbreaking
topics.summary: Shkreli demonstrated that copying a specific viral prompt causes ChatGPT to produce immersive sci-fi LARPing responses; discussed this as a new art form and the potential for personalized AI entertainment from media companies like Viacom.

topics.name: Stablecoin Integration into Big Tech
topics.summary: Kyle Samani argued post-Genius Act, it is now legal for iOS, Android, Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, and TikTok to embed stablecoins, and it is only a matter of time before they do, onboarding billions to crypto infrastructure.

topics.name: Slate EV Truck Challenges
topics.summary: The two-door Slate truck faces headwinds from EV tariff exposure that could raise its price 20–30% from ~$30K, undermining its value proposition against the Ford Maverick; American consumers historically prefer 4-door trucks 5:1.

topics.name: AI for Materials Science
topics.summary: Joseph Krause's unnamed startup raised a $55M seed to build the world's most advanced AI-powered materials R&D facility with autonomous robotics; argues AI has unlocked the ability to accelerate discovery across automotive, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor materials.
